subject: Post-demo recap: model fit suggestions + prompt capture request (Logosys)
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Alex Harper <alex.harper@logosys.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 19 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap: model fit suggestions + prompt capture request (Logosys)

Alex — thanks for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps to get the eval moving: 

- Summary: Your primary goal is an extractive Q&A assistant over internal product docs (mix of PDFs and Confluence pages) with strict PII redaction and a high precision preference for short factual answers. Latency target: 300ms median on single-request retrieval + generation. Scale: ~150 reqs/min peak.
- Initial Redwood model recommendations (for benching):
  * Redwood-Open-70B-v1 (fp16) — highest quality baseline for our eval set
  * Redwood-Quant-34B-q4_0 — lower-cost candidate with good tradeoffs for short answers
  * Redwood-Redline-13B-int8 — fallback for cost-sensitive endpoints and can be used for reranking

Links: we’ll run the Logosys eval on the Redwood benchmark harness. I’ll share the link and a short results dashboard once the runs start.

What we need from your side to proceed:
1) Prompt set + edge cases: a CSV of 200–300 representative prompts (both typical user queries and edge cases that are risky for hallucination or PII leakage). Please include the expected answer where possible.
2) Redaction guidance: explicit list of entity types to remove (SSNs, internal IDs, full names in some contexts). If Legal requires specific masking rules, please attach.
3) Data access plan: where the documents live (S3/Drive/Confluence) and a point of contact to grant read-only access to a test bundle.

I’m attaching a short prompt collection template (prompt_collection_template.csv) and a one-page redaction guidance example (redaction_guidance.pdf). If you can upload your sample prompts to the Drive folder I linked, we’ll intake them into the eval pipeline and return an initial quality/cost tradeoff report within 5 business days.

Next steps: can you confirm the target prompt delivery date? We can start benchmark runs as soon as we have ~150 prompts and doc access.

Thanks — Diego

--
Diego Fernandez
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
diego@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Harper <alex.harper@logosys.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
Cc: Logosys Legal <legal@logosys.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 10:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: model fit suggestions + prompt capture request (Logosys)

Hi Diego — appreciated the demo. Attaching a first-pass set of prompts (logosys_sample_prompts.csv) — ~120 rows that combine typical support questions, troubleshooting steps, and some red-team-style edge cases. A few notes:

- We included examples where users paste blocks of logs (very noisy) — those are high priority for redaction checks.
- We flagged examples that involve contract numbers and internal ticket IDs; Legal suggests masking contract numbers but would prefer case-by-case for tickets.
- We don’t yet have a consolidated Confluence export; SRE can produce a 10k-doc test bundle by EOD Friday if that works for you.

We can aim to get the full prompt CSV and the SRE export by next Friday (2026-07-24). Is that timeline compatible with your 5-business-day turnaround after ingestion? Also looping in our internal privacy lead (Legal is on cc) — they’ll send the formal redaction requirements if needed.

Thanks,
Alex

--
Alex Harper
Senior Product Manager, Logosys
alex.harper@logosys.com

From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Alex Harper <alex.harper@logosys.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: model fit suggestions + prompt capture request (Logosys)

Alex — this is great, thanks for the sample file. A few follow-ups before we kick off the harness: 

- Timeline: Friday 2026-07-24 for the 10k-doc bundle is fine. If you can drop an incremental 50–75 prompts earlier this week that would let us start a warm-up run and surface obvious regressions faster.
- Prompt format: please use the attached prompt_collection_template.csv columns exactly (prompt_id,prompt_text,expected_answer,edgecase_flag,notes). That helps automation and preserves expected_answer for quality scoring.
- Redaction: the one-page guidance is a starting point; if Legal can send explicit masking rules (e.g., mask SSN as [SSN_REDACTED], redact tokens longer than 9 digits, redact patterns matching internal-order-\d{6}) we’ll ensure the preprocessor enforces them. If Legal needs us to run a simulated redaction report prior to model runs, we can produce that.
- Benchmarks + what we’ll deliver: initial quality/cost table across the three model candidates I listed (the benchmark page link is here: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/logosys-eval-2026). We’ll include per-model latency percentiles, token cost estimates, and a short false-positive/false-negative breakdown for redaction regressions.

Action item for Logosys: upload the partial prompt set to the Drive folder and share SRE contact for test-bundle access. I’ll schedule the eval and send a kickoff calendar invite once we have the minimum prompt count (150).

Forwarding this to Monica and Ben for orchestration — Monica, can you take point on the first-run schedule and confirm we have capacity for a 150-prompt warm-up? Ben, can you confirm licensing/entitlement for a short Dedicated run if Logosys wants a cost/p95 SLA readout?

Best,
Diego

Alex — thanks for sending the sample prompts. Quick internal note and next steps on scheduling the eval runs: 

- Capacity: we have a 2-GPU warm-up shard available this week for a 150-prompt warm run; that will produce an initial quality table and latency percentiles for Redwood-Open-70B-v1 and Redwood-Quant-34B-q4_0.
- Dedicated sizing: Ben — if Logosys wants a dedicated SLA trial for p95 latency under 350ms, can you confirm if we can provision a 4-GPU Dedicated test cluster for two weeks under a trial entitlement?
- Upload instructions for Logosys: please place prompt CSV in the Drive folder and add a short README.txt with the SRE contact and a link to the Confluence export if available. If Legal wants a simulated redaction report before model runs, we’ll queue that as a pre-step (no extra infra cost).

Alex — once you drop the incremental prompts we’ll schedule the warm-up run and send the results (including the redaction regression CSV) back within 3 working days of ingestion. If you want an accelerated SLA-readout for the Dedicated cluster, Ben can coordinate pricing and entitlements.

Thanks — Monica
